credits.text: Chapter scenes written for this guide from the Coppermind's chapter summaries
Chapter routes adapted from Alton Chaney's Cosmere Maps (MIT)

summary.text: After a Desolation, Kalak found only Jezrien at the Heralds' meeting place, and the two left their Honorblades and the Oathpact behind as the others had, leaving Talenel alone.
On the night of a treaty feast with the Parshendi, Szeth, a Shin assassin in white, killed King Gavilar, who gave him a black sphere and a message for his brother Dalinar.
In Brightlord Amaram's army, the new recruit Cenn was saved in his first battle by his squadleader, Kaladin Stormblessed, until an enemy Shardbearer came.
Eight months later, Kaladin was a branded slave in Tvlakv's caravan, where a windspren began to talk to him.
Shallan landed in Kharbranth and climbed to the Conclave with the sailor Yalb, still chasing Jasnah Kholin.
When Tvlakv got lost, Kaladin refused to help, but the windspren spotted people ahead: the caravan was bound for the warcamps on the Shattered Plains.
Jasnah Soulcast a fallen stone to free King Taravangian's granddaughter, then turned Shallan down as her ward; Shallan's real aim was to steal Jasnah's Soulcaster.
Sold to Sadeas' army as a bridgeman, Kaladin survived his first bridge run, and the windspren told him her name: Sylphrena, or Syl.
Waiting in Jasnah's alcove at the Palanaeum, Shallan wrote her a letter and met Kabsal, an ardent hoping to convert Jasnah.
Won over by Shallan's self-taught studies and persistence, Jasnah took her as her ward.
Weeks into bridge duty, with nearly everyone from his first run dead, Kaladin sank into despair and Syl left him.
Nine years earlier in Hearthstone, young Kal helped his father, the surgeon Lirin, treat a girl's hand, and argued that soldiers could save lives too.
At the edge of a chasm after a highstorm, Kaladin chose not to jump when Syl came back to him.
Kaladin forced Gaz to make him bridgeleader of Bridge Four.
In the Purelake, the fisherman Ishikk told a group of foreigners that no village had seen the man they were looking for.
At the Davar estate, Shallan's brother Balat brooded over her mission until Wikim came to tell him of a big problem.
Szeth served Took, who showed off his obedience in mining towns, until thugs killed Took and took Szeth's Oathstone.
On a chasmfiend hunt with King Elhokar and Sadeas, Dalinar raced the king up a rock and, remembering a voice telling him to unite them, let him win.
When the chasmfiend came, Elhokar's saddle strap broke and Dalinar caught the beast's claw to save him, and Elhokar killed it.
Kaladin dragged Bridge Four out of bed to train; they refused, so he trained alone, running a bridge plank across the lumberyard.
After the hunt Adolin nearly came to blows with Sadeas, and Elhokar's broken strap was found to look cut.
Seven and a half years earlier, Kal lost a quarterstaff fight to Jost, then learned that the citylord, Wistiow, had died and left him spheres to study surgery in Kharbranth.
On a bridge run Kaladin ran at the front in Rock's place, then had Bridge Four carry its wounded home on the bridge.
Adolin heard that the king's strap had probably been cut, and asked the ardent Kadash about his father's fits in highstorms.
Dalinar asked Elhokar whether they should end the war, then suggested he be named Highprince of War.
Caught by a highstorm, Dalinar had a vision of saving a woman and her daughter from strange creatures until two Knights Radiant came to help.
Seven years earlier, Kal could not save an injured girl, and Lirin told him he had to learn when to care and when to let go.
When Sadeas cut off food and pay for wounded bridgemen, Kaladin asked Bridge Four to share; only Rock agreed, and he could see Syl.
At the king's feast Navani, Gavilar's widow, arrived unexpectedly, and Elhokar named Sadeas Highprince of Information to look into the cut strap.
On stone duty Kaladin, Rock and Teft gathered knobweed for its antiseptic sap, and Rock told how he came to be a bridgeman.
In the Gallery of Maps, Highprince Roion turned down Dalinar's offer of a joint plateau assault.
When Dalinar let Sadeas investigate in his camp because a vision told him to trust Sadeas, Adolin called the visions delusions.
Seven years earlier, Hearthstone's new citylord, Brightlord Roshone, arrived and blamed Lirin for Wistiow's death.
In a plateau battle Dalinar suddenly sickened of the killing and heard a voice say 'Life before death', then saw a Parshendi Shardbearer watching.
On chasm duty, scavenging from the dead, Kaladin picked up a spear and ran a kata that left Bridge Four staring.
Inspecting the camp, Dalinar learned that all eight other highprinces had refused to fight beside him.
After a spanreed talk with Jasnah, Dalinar told Navani he meant to abdicate.
In Shinovar, the young merchant Rysn watched her babsk Vstim trade with the Shin, among whom farmers outrank warriors.
In Kasitor, Axies the Collector saw the great spren Cusicesh rise from the bay, then was hauled off to jail.

summary.text: Sent by his master Makkek to kill a rival, Szeth found him already dead and a new master holding Makkek's head, Szeth's Oathstone and a list of noblemen to kill.
By spanreed, Balat warned Shallan that dangerous men claiming to be their father's friends wanted his Soulcaster back.
Sketching King Taravangian over lunch, Shallan drew strange figures with symbols for heads that weren't there.
Gaz paid part of his debt to Lamaril, who wanted Kaladin to die on a bridge run rather than be killed outright.
All of Bridge Four now trained with Kaladin, practising with their bridge.
Six years earlier, Lirin faced down a mob of villagers who believed he had stolen Wistiow's spheres.
Kaladin had Bridge Four carry their bridge on its side, saving them but drawing the fire onto the other crews, and Lamaril had him beaten.
Kabsal brought bread and jam and showed Shallan cymatics, and Jasnah warned her that he only wanted to get to Jasnah.
Lamaril was executed for the failed assault.
Kaladin was strung up outside the barrack to face a highstorm, and his men promised not to go back to how they were.
Kaladin lived through the highstorm clutching a sphere, which Teft saw had gone dun.

events.placeName: an alley in the lower city

summary.text: Jasnah led Shallan into a dark alley and killed the thugs who attacked them, and that night Shallan swapped Jasnah's Soulcaster for the broken one she had brought.
Five and a half years earlier, Roshone demanded most of Wistiow's spheres from Lirin, and his son Rillir treated Kal like a servant.
As Kaladin lay in a fever, Teft, raised among the Envisagers, put spheres in his hand and watched Stormlight heal him.
Shallan caught herself drawing a man lying dead in a pool of blood, and Balat told her that their father's friends had come back.
Back on his feet, Kaladin saw that bridgemen were bait for Parshendi arrows, and Bridge Four gave Rock a razor for his stew.
Five and a half years earlier, Lirin couldn't save Roshone's son Rillir after a whitespine attack, but saved Roshone.
The stolen Soulcaster wouldn't work for Shallan, a voice asked what she was, and she found Jasnah's notes on Urithiru and the Voidbringers.
Lamaril's replacement, Matal, and his wife Hashal put Bridge Four on chasm duty for good.
Five years earlier, when Brightlord Amaram came recruiting, Roshone had Tien drafted, and Kaladin enlisted to protect him.
Chased by the symbol-headed figures, Shallan slipped into a place of glass beads and turned a goblet into blood, then cut herself to hide it from Jasnah.
Kaladin dreamt he rode a highstorm across Roshar and heard a voice warn that Odium was coming, and a parshman the men called Shen joined Bridge Four.
A year earlier, in his last battle for Amaram, Kaladin saw Cenn and most of his squad cut down by an enemy Shardbearer, then killed the Shardbearer and refused the Shards.
Kept in hospital after cutting herself, Shallan ate Kabsal's bread; he collapsed, she was poisoned, and she gave Jasnah the stolen Soulcaster to save her.
Down in the chasms Kaladin began training Bridge Four with spears, and Teft showed he had been a soldier.
Jasnah told Shallan that Kabsal had poisoned the bread to kill Jasnah, and that the theft had thrown away Shallan's future as a scholar.
A year earlier, Amaram had Kaladin's last four men killed, took the Shards for himself and had Kaladin branded a slave.

events.placeName: the palace of Ashno of Sages

summary.text: Baxil and his cousin Av watched their mistress destroy the art in the palace of Ashno of Sages.
The ardent Geranid found that a flamespren stopped changing once she measured it, as if it knew.
Szeth stormed King Hanavanar's banquet in Vedenar and killed the king and his Shardbearers.
In a vision Dalinar watched Knights Radiant abandon their Shards, and afterwards Renarin suggested asking Jasnah to check the visions' details.
Dunny was killed on a bridge run, and Kaladin had Bridge Four start saving the wounded from other crews.
At a feast Sadeas announced that the strap had been cut inside the king's palace grounds, and agreed to Dalinar's offer to join forces.
Dalinar and Sadeas made their first joint plateau assault, and won it quickly.
In the chasms Bridge Four found an emerald broam on a dead officer, and Rock shot it up on an arrow to hide under a bridge.
When a second Parshendi army struck, Dalinar fought his way to the fallen Sadeas and held them off until Adolin came.
After Maps died, Teft tricked Kaladin into drawing in Stormlight, and Syl admitted she wasn't a windspren.
Wit played the flute for Kaladin, told him the story of the Wandersail and gave him the flute.
Drinking in the Outer Market with friends, Adolin began to see the sense in his father's strict ways.
While Adolin won a duel, Elhokar had Dalinar agree to a joint assault with Sadeas using both armies' bridge crews.
Hashal put Bridge Four on bridge runs by day and chasm duty by night, a death sentence.
In the chasms Kaladin used Stormlight to climb a wall and tie a sack of Parshendi carapace under a bridge, then dropped forty feet unhurt.
In a vision Dalinar met Nohadon, author of The Way of Kings, and Navani realised he had been speaking the Dawnchant, proof the visions were real.
Navani told Dalinar why she had come back and they kissed, and she said the King of Jah Keved had been killed by a Shin Shardbearer in white.
Wearing Parshendi carapace, Kaladin drew the archers' fire onto his shield, and later Dalinar charged a band of Parshendi archers aiming at Bridge Four.
Kaladin had Leyten make carapace armour for every bridgeman but Shen, and Moash said he wanted vengeance.
Dalinar told Navani he had once stepped aside so Gavilar could court her.
Bridge Four lined up in carapace armour and bone shields, and the other crews cheered them.
Dalinar and Sadeas set out with fifteen thousand troops to finish the Parshendi at the Tower.
At the Tower, Kaladin led the decoys that drew Parshendi arrows away from the bridges.
Dalinar's army fought its way onto the Tower, until he saw that Sadeas had pulled out and left him surrounded.
Kaladin saw that Sadeas was retreating on purpose, betraying Dalinar.
Cut off, Dalinar told his men they would die with their honour intact.
Sadeas' army withdrew west, leaving Bridge Four behind.
Kaladin remembered how Tien died, sent to the front as bait in his first battle.
Syl remembered she was an honorspren, and Kaladin led Bridge Four back to bridge a way out for Dalinar's army.
Glowing with Stormlight, Kaladin held the bridge with Bridge Four and saved Dalinar from a Parshendi Shardbearer, then agreed to join his army.
Told that Dalinar had fallen, Navani burned a huge glyph for justice into Sadeas' staging ground just before word came that he lived.
Dalinar traded his Shardblade to Sadeas for the freedom of all Sadeas' bridgemen.
Dalinar beat Elhokar in a scuffle, got him to admit he had cut his own strap, and told him to name Dalinar Highprince of War.
Shallan worked out that Jasnah's Soulcaster was fake, went back to the place of beads to prove it, and Jasnah agreed to teach her.
Szeth came to kill King Taravangian, the last name on his list, and found the king was his master, who added Dalinar Kholin to the list.
Jasnah's notes led Shallan to see that the Voidbringers had not been destroyed but enslaved, as the parshmen.
Dalinar made Kaladin a captain with Bridge Four as his guard, and the men asked Kaladin to teach them his powers.
Shallan and Jasnah planned to sail for the Shattered Plains, and Jasnah named Kabsal a Ghostblood, a group Shallan realised her father had likely belonged to.
In a last vision Dalinar learned the voice had never heard him; it told him to refound the Knights Radiant and said the Almighty was dead, killed by Odium.
In Kholinar, Wit was talking with the guards when Talenel staggered in with a Shardblade, warned of a coming Desolation and collapsed.
Joshor of the king's Silent Gatherers wrote down a dying Herdazian's ketek and left its meaning for the king.
